correctness.rationale: Testing the constant target a^k after deleting an a forces at least k+1 copies of each letter, hence |w|≥q(k+1); k+1 complete permutation blocks attain it. At equality, write a_i for occurrence i. For distinct a,b, delete b_{k+1} and require a^i b^(k-i) for 1≤i≤k-1, forcing a_i<b_(i+1). For i=k, delete a_1 and require a^(k-1)b, forcing a_k<b_(k+1). Interchange a,b; occurrence levels are globally ordered, hence each consecutive block is a permutation. For k=1 every double-multiplicity arrangement survives deletion. Independent literal subsequence tests exhausted multiset words at (q,k)=(2,1..4),(3,1..2), matching counts 6,8,16,32,90,216; infinite result is the occurrence proof, not experiments.

value.rationale: One erasure is a canonical robustness perturbation of subsequence universality. The result gives a complete infinite family of minimal resilient hosts and a sharp rigidity boundary at target length two, with exact enumerations rather than just existence.

final_claim: On q≥2 labeled symbols, shortest words remaining k-subsequence-universal under deletion of any single position have length q(k+1). At k≥2 they are exactly concatenations of k+1 alphabet permutations, counted by (q!)^(k+1); for k=1 all double-multiplicity arrangements qualify, counted by (2q)!/2^q.
limitations: Scattered subsequences, one arbitrary deleted position, labeled alphabet; longer hosts not classified.
residual_risks: A short corollary in a broad arch-factorization or edited-universality paper might give the same rigidity without wording it as resilience.
